<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:0.12in; text-indent:-0.12in;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>&#62; During the fiscal half-year ended June 30, 2006, Vanguard 500 Index Fund, like its benchmark, retreated in the second quarter after performing strongly in the first quarter.</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:0.12in; text-indent:-0.12in;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>&#62; The fund&#146;s Investor Shares gained 2.6% during the six months (the Admiral Shares returned 2.7%), in line with the fund&#146;s benchmark index. </font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:0.12in; text-indent:-0.12in;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>&#62; Solid performances within the index&#146;s energy and industrials sectors were offset by losses in the poorly performing health care and information technology sectors. </font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>Chairman&#146;s Letter</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Dear Shareholder,</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>For the six months ended June 30, 2006, Vanguard 500 Index Fund&#146;s Investor Shares returned 2.6% and the Admiral Shares returned 2.7%, as the U.S. stock market climbed steadily, then drifted backward. The alignment of the fund&#146;s result with that of the index benchmark, the Standard &amp; Poor&#146;s 500 Index, was an accomplishment that reflects the fund&#146;s superior trading and portfolio-construction methodologies and its consistently low expenses. For the period, the fund topped the average performance of large-capitalization core funds by more than 1 percentage point.</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Stocks started strongly, then retreated on inflation concerns</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The U.S. stock market climbed from January into early May, taking its cues from healthy economic data, strong corporate earnings, and historically low unemployment rates. In a strange twist, these positive dynamics helped to nudge the market off track in mid-May, as investors feared that the economy&#151;and inflationary pressures&#151;had gained too much steam. The broad U.S. market lost roughly half of its 2006 gains in a volatile May and June, but still returned about 3.5% for the half-year.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>International equities traced a similar path, though their highs were generally higher and the declines, greater. As a group, they outpaced U.S. stocks for the half-year, with European stocks performing particularly well.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Bonds struggled to maintain footing as interest rates climbed</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The Federal Reserve Board raised its target for the federal funds rate four times during the period, to 5.25%, marking the 17th consecutive rate hike since the central bank began its inflation-fighting campaign two years ago. The broad market for taxable U.S. bonds finished the six months with a modestly negative return, while municipal bond returns were modestly positive. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Yields of U.S. Treasury securities rose at both ends of the maturity spectrum, but the yield curve remained relatively flat, with only 20 basis points separating the yields of the shortest- and longest-term issues. High-yield bonds were one of the better-performing segments of a stagnant fixed income market. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Losses in May and June minimized the fund&#146;s six-month return</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The 2.6% return of the 500 Index Fund&#146;s Investor Shares for the fiscal half-year closely tracked the performance of the S&amp;P 500 Index. The fund&#146;s showing echoed investor sentiment, which was bullish through the first four months of the year, then increasingly bearish in May and June as inflation fears&#151;and volatility&#151;increased.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

            <p style='margin-left:0pt;text-indent:0pt;text-align:right;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt'><font size=2>4.3%</font></p> </td>
        <td width="96" valign=top style='border-bottom:solid black 1.0pt;  '>
            <p style='margin-left:0pt;text-indent:0pt;text-align:right;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt'><font size=2>2.7%</font></p> </td> </tr></table>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:center;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The energy and industrials sectors produced healthy returns during the six months. As energy supplies continued to be tight and prices increased, big oil firms such as ExxonMobil, ConocoPhillips, and Chevron earned robust returns. In the industrials sector, both Caterpillar and Textron were standout performers. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Another bright spot for the index was the telecommunication services sector. Although the sector represents only 3% of the index&#146;s holdings, it was up 14% during the six months. Firms such as BellSouth and Qwest Communications advanced steadily, bolstering relatively weak returns of other sectors.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Concerns about the sustainability of strong consumer spending in the face of rising short-term interest rates and surging energy prices weighed on the retailers and entertainment companies that make up the consumer discretionary sector, which gained 2.6%, on par with the fund&#146;s overall performance. The financial services sector, the index&#146;s largest weighting, gained 3%. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The index&#146;s information technology and health care sectors both declined. Among IT companies, both earnings and corporate spending continued to disappoint. Industry giants Intel and Microsoft both reported lackluster earnings for the period.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Ignoring today&#146;s ups and downs can give you a long-term focus</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Successful long-term investing doesn&#146;t mean paying attention to today&#146;s headlines, chasing yesterday&#146;s performance, or trying to predict what</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
<font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>Notes to Financial Statements</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Vanguard 500 Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers two classes of shares, Investor Shares and Admiral Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>A.</font></B><font size=2> The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid
prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>5. Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:center;'><font size=2>19</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Liquidity Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>6. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>B.</font></B><font size=2> The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital contributions to Vanguard. At June 30, 2006, the fund had contributed capital of $11,792,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 11.79% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>C.</font></B><font size=2> Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes; these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>During the six months ended June 30, 2006, the fund realized $314,329,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized gains to paid-in capital.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The fund&#146;s tax-basis capital gains and losses are determined only at the end of each fiscal year. For tax purposes, at December 31, 2005, the fund had available realized losses of $5,517,969,000 to offset future net capital gains of $193,358,000 through December 31, 2008, $890,248,000 through December 31, 2009, $3,087,963,000 through December 31, 2010, $145,498,000 through December 31, 2011, $44,874,000 through December 31, 2012, $757,853,000 through December 31, 2013, and $398,175,000 through December 31, 2014.  The fund will use these capital losses to offset net taxable capital gains, if any, realized during the year ending December 31, 2006; should the fund realize net capital losses for the year, the losses will be added to the loss carryforward balances above.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>About Your Fund&#146;s Expenses</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The table below illustrates your fund&#146;s costs in two ways: </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>&#149; Based on actual fund return.</font></b><font size=2> This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &#147;Ending Account Value&#148; shown is derived from the fund&#146;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>To do so, simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#147;Expenses Paid During Period.&#148; </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>&#149; Based on hypothetical 5% yearly return.</font></b><font size=2> This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#146;s costs with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#151;because the return used is not the fund&#146;s actual return&#151;the results do not apply to your investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&#146;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>Trustees Approve Advisory Arrangement</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The board of trustees of Vanguard 500 Index Fund has approved the fund&#146;s investment advisory arrangement with The Vanguard Group, Inc. Vanguard&#151;through its Quantitative Equity Group&#151;serves as the investment advisor for the fund. The board determined that continuing the fund&#146;s internalized management structure was in the best interests of the fund and its shareholders.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The board based its decision upon its most recent evaluation of the advisor&#146;s investment staff, portfolio management process, and performance. The trustees considered the factors discussed below, among others. However, no single factor determined whether the board approved the arrangement. Rather, it was the totality of the circumstances that drove the board&#146;s decision.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Nature, extent, and quality of services</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The board considered the quality of the fund&#146;s investment management over both short- and long-term periods, and took into account the organizational depth and stability of the advisor. Vanguard has been managing investments for more than two decades. George U. Sauter, Vanguard managing director and chief investment officer, has been in the investment management business since 1985. Mr. Sauter has led the Quantitative Equity Group since 1987. The Quantitative Equity Group adheres to a sound, disciplined investment management process; the team has considerable experience, stability, and depth.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The board concluded that Vanguard&#146;s experience, stability, depth, and performance, among other factors, warranted continuation of the advisory arrangement.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Investment performance</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The board considered the short- and long-term performance of the fund, including any periods of outperformance or underperformance of a relevant benchmark and peer group. The board noted that the fund has performed in line with expectations, and that its results have been consistent with its investment strategies. Information about the fund&#146;s performance, including some of the data considered by the board, can be found in the Performance Summary section of this report.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Cost</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The 500 Index Fund&#146;s expense ratio was far below the average expense ratio charged by funds in its peer group. The fund&#146;s advisory expense ratio was also well below its peer-group average. Information about the fund&#146;s expense ratio appears in the About Your Fund&#146;s Expenses section of this report as well as in the Financial Statements section.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The board does not conduct a profitability analysis of Vanguard because of Vanguard&#146;s unique &#147;at-cost&#148; structure. Unlike most other mutual fund management companies, Vanguard is owned by the funds it oversees, and produces &#147;profits&#148; only in the form of reduced expenses for fund shareholders.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>The benefit of economies of scale</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The board of trustees concluded that Vanguard 500 Index Fund&#146;s low-cost arrangement with Vanguard ensures that the fund will realize economies of scale as it grows, with the cost to shareholders declining as fund assets increase.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The board will consider whether to renew the advisory arrangement again after a one-year period.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:center;'><font size=2>24</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>Glossary </font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Beta</font></b><font size=2>. A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell by 10%. A fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared (see definition below). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of volatility.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Earnings Growth Rate.</font></b><font size=2> The average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a fund.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Expense Ratio.</font></b><font size=2> The percentage of a fund&#146;s average net assets used to pay its annual administrative and advisory expenses. These expenses directly reduce returns to investors.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Foreign Holdings.</font></b><font size=2> The percentage of a fund represented by stocks or depositary receipts of companies based outside the United States.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Median Market Cap.</font></b><font size=2> An indicator of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization (market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Price/Book Ratio.</font></b><font size=2> The share price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Price/Earnings Ratio.</font></b><font size=2> The ratio of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund, the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations for a company&#146;s future growth.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>R-Squared.</font></b><font size=2> A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Return on Equity.</font></b><font size=2> The annual average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Short-Term Reserves.</font></b><font size=2> The percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily converted to cash.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Turnover Rate.</font></b><font size=2> An indication of the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on costs.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Yield.</font></b><font size=2> A snapshot of a fund&#146;s income from interest and dividends. The yield, expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s net asset value, is based on income earned over the past 30 days and is annualized, or projected forward for the coming year. The index yield is based on the current annualized rate of income provided by securities in the index.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:center;'><font size=2>25</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>The People Who Govern Your Fund</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The trustees of your mutual fund are there to see that the fund is operated and managed in your best interests since, as a shareholder, you are a part owner of the fund. Your fund&#146;s trustees also serve on the board of directors of The Vanguard Group, Inc., which is owned by the Vanguard funds and provides services to them on an at-cost basis.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>A majority of Vanguard&#146;s board members are independent, meaning that they have no affiliation with Vanguard or the funds they oversee, apart from the sizable personal investments they have made as private individuals. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Our independent board members bring distinguished backgrounds in business, academia, and public service to their task of working with Vanguard officers to establish the policies and oversee the activities of the funds. Among board members&#146; responsibilities are selecting investment advisors for the funds; monitoring fund operations, performance, and costs; reviewing contracts; nominating and selecting new trustees/directors; and electing Vanguard officers. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Each trustee serves a fund until its termination; or until the trustee&#146;s retirement, resignation, or death; or otherwise as specified in the fund&#146;s organizational documents. Any trustee may be removed at a shareholders&#146; meeting by a vote representing two-thirds of the net asset value of all shares of the fund together with shares of other Vanguard funds organized within the same trust. The table on these two pages shows information for each trustee and executive officer of the fund. The mailing address of the trustees and officers is P.O. Box 876, Valley Forge, PA 19482.  </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>1</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:1.17%; text-indent:-1.17%;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'> <IMG SRC="jack.gif"> <br> </p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=3>Chairman&#146;s Letter</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Dear Shareholder,</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.15pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=2>In the first half of 2006, small-company stocks outperformed the broad U.S. stock market, and value-oriented stocks outpaced growth stocks. Vanguard&#146;s small-capitalization index funds achieved their objectives of closely tracking their indexes. Investor Shares of the Vanguard Small-Cap Index Fund returned 6.9% and kept pace with the average return of competing funds. Investor Shares of the Small-Cap Growth Index Fund and Small-Cap Value Index fund returned 5.7% and 8.0%, respectively; both funds outpaced the average returns of competitors.</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Stocks started strongly, then retreated on inflation concerns </font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The U.S. stock market climbed from January into early May, taking its cues from healthy economic data, strong corporate earnings, and historically low unemployment rates. In a strange twist, these positive dynamics helped to nudge the market off track in mid-May, as investors feared that the economy&#151;and inflationary pressures&#151;had gained too much steam. The broad U.S. market lost roughly half of its 2006 gains in a volatile May and June, but still returned about 3.5% for the half-year.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>International equities traced a similar path, though their highs were generally higher and the declines, greater. As a group, they outpaced U.S. stocks for the half-year, with European stocks performing particularly well.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>2</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Bonds struggled to maintain footing as interest rates climbed</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The Federal Reserve Board raised its target for the federal funds rate four times during the period, to 5.25%, marking the 17th consecutive rate hike since the central bank began its inflation-fighting campaign two years ago. The broad market for taxable U.S. bonds finished the six months with a modestly negative return, while municipal bond returns were modestly positive. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.15pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Yields of U.S. Treasury securities rose at both ends of the maturity spectrum, but the yield curve remained relatively flat, with only 20 basis points separating the yields of the shortest- and longest-term issues. High-yield bonds were one of the better-performing segments of a stagnant fixed income market. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Industrials, materials, and energy posted admirable returns</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Small-cap stocks enjoyed much stronger returns than the overall U.S. market in the first four months of 2006. The stock market&#146;s retreat in May and June, however, hit small-caps particularly hard. Still, the advances that smaller stocks made in the early part of the year were sufficient to keep them ahead of the broad market at the midpoint. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Most of the industry groups represented in the Vanguard Small-Cap Index Funds recorded positive returns during the half-year.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>3</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
<font size=2>The differences in the three funds&#146; returns resulted from the portfolios&#146; different weightings in various industry sectors, some of which did better than others.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>During the period, several historically value-oriented segments performed impressively. The economy&#146;s less glamorous sectors&#151;materials, industrials, and energy&#151;posted double-digit returns. Telecommunication services also recorded excellent results, although its small weighting (about 1% in each of the indexes) meant that its impact was minor. Weaker sectors included health care, information technology, and consumer discretionary&#151;all traditional growth areas.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The Small-Cap Value Index Fund, with a return of 8.0% for its Investor Shares, benefited from the strength in industrials, materials, and energy stocks. The fund&#146;s leading contributor, however, was the financials sector, which made up more than a third of the portfolio and returned 7.5%. Real estate investment trusts drove the bulk of this sector&#146;s gain.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The Small-Cap Growth Index Fund, which returned 5.7% for the Investor Shares, also benefited from exposure to energy and industrials stocks. However, the fund was hampered by poor performance in its largest sectors&#151;information technology, </font></p>

<font size=2>health care, and consumer discretionary&#151;which together accounted for more than 50% of the fund&#146;s assets.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The Small-Cap Index Fund is essentially a blend of the other two funds, and its half-year return&#151;6.9% for both Investor and Admiral Shares&#151;fell between theirs.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.15pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>All three Small-Cap Index Funds closely tracked their target indexes, a tribute to the skills of the investment advisor, Vanguard Quantitative Equity Group. The advisor&#146;s job was made easier by Vanguard&#146;s low expense ratios, which allow a greater portion of each fund&#146;s total return to go to shareholders.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Diversification can smooth volatility within your portfolio</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Small-cap stocks have historically experienced higher volatility than large-caps, as the fortune of a small company often hinges on the success&#151;or failure&#151;of a narrow set of products or services. Larger companies, by contrast, tend to have broader and more diverse lines of products and services. When one of those lines does poorly, others can often pick up the slack. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>You can draw a parallel in your own investment plan. Recently, small-cap stocks have been one of the better-performing segments of the market. But building a portfolio that relies too heavily on one part of the market could be the equivalent of a bad business plan. A portfolio that is balanced and diversified among stock, bond, and money market funds can help you endure the inevitable bumps in the road. The Vanguard Small-Cap Index Funds can serve as an intelligent way to broaden and diversify your portfolio.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:18.6pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=3>Notes to Financial Statements</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Vanguard Small-Cap Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and ETF Shares. ETF Shares were known as VIPER Shares prior to July 6, 2006. The name change to ETF Shares has been reflected throughout these financial statements. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria. Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative and servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. ETF Shares are listed for trading on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through a broker.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>A.</font></B><font size=2> The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid
prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Net Assets </font></i><font size=2>as an asset (liability) and in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Operations </font></i><font size=2>as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;'><font size=2>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>20</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:22.95pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:58.5%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=1>Vanguard Small-Cap Index Fund</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>5. Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>6. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>B.</font></B><font size=2> The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital contributions to Vanguard. At June 30, 2006, the fund had contributed capital of $1,351,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 1.35% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>C.</font></B><font size=2> Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes; these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>During the six months ended June 30, 2006, the fund realized $414,392,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized gains to paid-in capital.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The fund&#146;s tax-basis capital gains and losses are determined only at the end of each fiscal year. For tax purposes, at December 31, 2005, the fund had available realized losses of $385,074,000 to offset future net capital gains of $347,890,000 through December 31, 2011, and $37,184,000 through December 31, 2014. The fund will use these capital losses to offset net taxable capital gains, if any, realized during the year ending December 31, 2006; should the fund realize net capital losses for the year, the losses will be added to the loss carryforward balances above.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>At June 30, 2006, net unrealized appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was $3,019,964,000, consisting of unrealized gains of $3,537,523,000 on securities that had risen in value since their purchase and $517,559,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value since their purchase.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:22.95pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:52.33%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=1>Vanguard Small-Cap Growth Index Fund</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:18.6pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=3>Notes to Financial Statements</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Vanguard Small-Cap Growth Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, Institutional Shares, and ETF Shares. ETF Shares were known as VIPER Shares prior to July 6, 2006. The name change to ETF Shares has been reflected throughout these financial statements. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative and servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. ETF Shares are listed for trading on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through a broker.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>A.</font></B><font size=2> The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid
prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Net Assets </font></i><font size=2>as an asset (liability) and in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Operations </font></i><font size=2>as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;'><font size=2>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>33</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:56.95pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=1>Vanguard Small-Cap Growth Index Fund</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>5. Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>6. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>B.</font></B><font size=2> The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital contributions to Vanguard. At June 30, 2006, the fund had contributed capital of $292,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 0.29% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>C.</font></B><font size=2> Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes; these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>During the six months ended June 30, 2006, the fund realized $90,049,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized gains to paid-in capital.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The fund&#146;s tax-basis capital gains and losses are determined only at the end of each fiscal year. For tax purposes, at December 31, 2005, the fund had available realized losses of $29,145,000 to offset future net capital gains of $13,814,000 through December 31, 2011, and $15,331,000 through December 31, 2014. The fund will use these capital losses to offset net taxable capital gains, if any, realized during the year ending December 31, 2006; should the fund realize net capital losses for the year, the losses will be added to the loss carryforward balances above.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:22.95pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=1>Vanguard Small-Cap Value Index Fund</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:18.6pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=3>Notes to Financial Statements</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Vanguard Small-Cap Value Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, Institutional Shares, and ETF Shares. ETF Shares were known as VIPER Shares prior to July 6, 2006. The name change to ETF Shares has been reflected throughout these financial statements. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative and servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. ETF Shares are listed for trading on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through a broker.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>A.</font></B><font size=2> The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid
prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Net Assets </font></i><font size=2>as an asset (liability) and in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Operations </font></i><font size=2>as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>5. Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>46</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:56.95pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:53.83%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=1>Vanguard Small-Cap Value Index Fund</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;'><font size=2>Liquidity Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>6. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>B.</font></B><font size=2> The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital contributions to Vanguard. At June 30, 2006, the fund had contributed capital of $472,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 0.47% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>C.</font></B><font size=2> Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes; these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>During the six months ended June 30, 2006, the fund realized $185,286,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized gains to paid-in capital.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The fund&#146;s tax-basis capital gains and losses are determined only at the end of each fiscal year. For tax purposes, at December 31, 2005, the fund had available realized losses of $67,918,000 to offset future net capital gains through December 31, 2011. The fund will use these capital losses to offset net taxable capital gains, if any, realized during the year ending December 31, 2006; should the fund realize net capital losses for the year, the losses will be added to the loss carryforward balance above.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>At June 30, 2006, net unrealized appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was $700,770,000, consisting of unrealized gains of $839,981,000 on securities that had risen in value since their purchase and $139,211,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value since their purchase.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>E.</font></B><font size=2> The market value of securities on loan to broker-dealers at June 30, 2006, was $98,335,000, for which the fund received cash collateral of $104,414,000.</font></p>
